title: Exact 33 km depths had mixed assignment labels in 20 global M5.5+ ComCat events in 2013-2025
abstract: We tested whether exact depth labels and small reported vertical errors replace a depth-method field in a global ComCat snapshot. The CSV and preferred-origin QuakeML inputs agree on depths for 12,848 M5.5+ events in 2000-2025. No preferred XML origin has depthType. A stratified hash sample of 195 GeoJSON origin products has depth-type for 185 events. All 20 late-period events at exactly 33 km were checked: four have operator-assigned labels, 15 have waveform-model labels and one has a location label. In the full sample, 50 of 85 records with reported vertical error at most 2 km are operator assigned. Exact labels and small errors thus do not give the same information as an explicit method field in these checked groups. These are catalog metadata counts, not validated true depths or a physical depth trend. The sample is not proportional to global event frequency. Original code, aggregate counts, source hashes, external retrieval scripts, a figure and an independent count audit are supplied. External records remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Assignment labels by sampled depth group and era, and method-field availability by export. Early is 2000-2012; late is 2013-2025. Counts above bars are numerator/denominator. The 20 late 33 km events form a full group census; other bars use 25 sampled events each. Unweighted sample fractions do not estimate global frequencies.

citations.reason: Same CSV snapshot and era split. We add explicit method metadata rather than new depth-change bounds.
Stanley error-cut and six-case interface audit motivate the global metadata census and sample.
